slides.say: a and b are positive integers. a has exactly two prime factors, two and three. b has exactly two prime factors, two and five. Given: b is smaller than a. What is the smallest possible value of a times b, over fifteen?

A minimum question, with primes. a is built from twos and threes, and b from twos and fives. And b has to be smaller than a. [short pause] We'll solve it two ways, building the smallest a and b, and then plugging in the answers, starting from the smallest.
[short pause] When is a times b over fifteen smallest? a and b are both on top of the fraction, so the smaller they are, the smaller the result. So let's build each one as small as possible.

a has exactly the prime factors two and three. Exactly means both of them must be there, and nothing else. The smallest is one two and one three. Two times three is six. And b has two and five, so the smallest is two times five, which is ten.
at: two times five, which is ten

slides.say: But wait, b has to be smaller than a, and ten isn't smaller than six. Can b get smaller than ten? No, it needs a two and a five. So we have to grow a.
at: b has to be smaller than a

slides.say: By how much? a can only contain twos and threes, so I can multiply it by two, or by three. Six times two is twelve, and six times three is eighteen. To keep it as small as possible, times two. Twelve is bigger than ten, it works.

So a is twelve and b is ten. Twelve times ten is a hundred twenty, and a hundred twenty over fifteen is eight. Or with primes, two squared times three, times two times five, over three times five. The three and the five cancel, and two cubed is eight. Choice number one is our answer.
at: Choice number one is our answer

slides.say: And every other choice is a trap. Four is six times ten over fifteen, it forgets that b is smaller than a. Twelve grows a by three instead of two, eighteen times ten over fifteen. And sixteen grows b instead, twelve times twenty over fifteen.
at: every other choice is a trap

slides.say: [pause] Now let's try plugging in the answers. Each choice gives the value of the whole fraction, a times b divided by fifteen. They ask for the smallest, so start from the smallest choice, four. Multiply four by fifteen to find the product a times b that we need. Four times fifteen is sixty.

a is made of twos and threes, both of them, so a is six, twelve, eighteen, twenty-four and so on. And b is ten, twenty, forty, fifty and so on. Which pair multiplies to sixty? Only six times ten. But then b isn't smaller than a. So four is out.

Next, eight. a times b is eight times fifteen, which is a hundred twenty. Twelve times ten is a hundred twenty, and ten is smaller than twelve. It works. So the smallest possible value is eight, choice number one. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
